scenes.tts: How do you find the genes that let an axon cross only once? Look at the nerve cord of a fly embryo.
scenes.visual: Title card: Reading the Ladder. A fly embryo, then a zoom into its ventral nerve cord.
scenes.narration: How do you find the genes that let an axon cross only once? Look at the nerve cord of a fly embryo.

scenes.tts: Stained for its axons, the nerve cord looks like a ladder. Two long rails run the length of the body.
scenes.visual: Stained fly nerve cord drawn as a ladder: two bright longitudinal rails. Label: rails.
scenes.narration: Stained for its axons, the nerve cord looks like a ladder. Two long rails run the length of the body.

scenes.tts: In each segment, two rungs cross between them. These rungs are the commissures.
scenes.visual: Two rungs per segment highlight in turn. Label: commissures.
scenes.narration: In each segment, two rungs cross between them. These rungs are the commissures.

scenes.tts: Most commissural axons cross once, turn, and run in a rail on the far side.
scenes.visual: One axon traced in colour: crosses a rung, turns, joins the far rail.
scenes.narration: Most commissural axons cross once, turn, and run in a rail on the far side.

scenes.tts: In 1993, Corey Goodman's laboratory reported a screen for mutations that disturb this ladder.
scenes.visual: Names and year on screen (Seeger, Tear, Ferres-Marco, Goodman, 1993) beside rows of embryos being scored.
scenes.narration: In 1993, Corey Goodman's laboratory reported a screen for mutations that disturb this ladder.

scenes.tts: The screen recovered loss-of-function mutants, in which a gene's activity is reduced or lost. These were strong losses.
scenes.visual: Label: loss-of-function = gene activity reduced or abolished. Examples here: strong loss of function.
scenes.narration: The screen recovered loss-of-function mutants, in which a gene's activity is reduced or lost. These were strong losses.

scenes.tts: Before looking, set up the logic. The midline makes a repellent. Axons carry a receptor for it. Something in the axon sets when the receptor works.
scenes.visual: Logic diagram: midline emits repellent; axon carries a receptor; a clock icon on the axon labelled timing.
scenes.narration: Before looking, set up the logic. The midline makes a repellent. Axons carry a receptor for it. Something in the axon sets when the receptor works.

scenes.tts: First case. Axons lose their main receptor for the repellent. What does the ladder look like?
scenes.visual: Logic diagram with the main receptor crossed out; a smaller second receptor stays on the axon. Question mark over a blank ladder.
scenes.narration: First case. Axons lose their main receptor for the repellent. What does the ladder look like?

scenes.tts: Little holds axons off the midline. Ipsilateral axons cross. Commissural axons cross and then cross back. The rungs thicken.
scenes.visual: Reveal: a ladder with thick rungs; one traced axon crosses and crosses back.
scenes.narration: Little holds axons off the midline. Ipsilateral axons cross. Commissural axons cross and then cross back. The rungs thicken.

scenes.tts: This is the mutant called roundabout, or robo. Its axons circle back across.
scenes.visual: Label: roundabout (robo).
scenes.narration: This is the mutant called roundabout, or robo. Its axons circle back across.

scenes.tts: Second case. The midline makes no repellent. Predict the ladder.
scenes.visual: Logic diagram with the repellent crossed out. Blank ladder, question mark.
scenes.narration: Second case. The midline makes no repellent. Predict the ladder.

scenes.tts: The repellent's push is gone, so axons that reach the midline are not pushed out. They enter and do not leave.
scenes.visual: Reveal: axons pile into the midline.
scenes.narration: The repellent's push is gone, so axons that reach the midline are not pushed out. They enter and do not leave.

scenes.tts: Over time the two rails collapse into a single bundle down the middle. This is the slit mutant.
scenes.visual: The two rails merge into one bundle along the midline. Label: slit.
scenes.narration: Over time the two rails collapse into a single bundle down the middle. This is the slit mutant.

scenes.tts: Third case. Commissural axons have a working receptor before they cross. What now?
scenes.visual: Logic diagram with the timing clock set to early. Blank ladder, question mark.
scenes.narration: Third case. Commissural axons have a working receptor before they cross. What now?

scenes.tts: They are pushed away before they can cross. Almost no axon crosses, and the rungs nearly vanish.
scenes.visual: Reveal: two rails with almost no rungs.
scenes.narration: They are pushed away before they can cross. Almost no axon crosses, and the rungs nearly vanish.

scenes.tts: This is commissureless, or comm. The name says it: the rungs are nearly gone.
scenes.visual: Label: commissureless (comm). The three mutant ladders sit side by side.
scenes.narration: This is commissureless, or comm. The name says it: the rungs are nearly gone.

scenes.tts: In 1998, Thomas Kidd, Tear, Goodman and colleagues cloned robo. It encodes a receptor that spans the membrane once.
scenes.visual: A single-pass receptor drawn in a membrane, outer domains labelled Ig. Label: Robo, 1998.
scenes.narration: In 1998, Thomas Kidd, Tear, Goodman and colleagues cloned robo. It encodes a receptor that spans the membrane once.

scenes.tts: Its timing was the telling part. Axons that never cross carry Robo on their growth cones from the start.
scenes.visual: An ipsilateral growth cone with Robo receptors on it from the beginning.
scenes.narration: Its timing was the telling part. Axons that never cross carry Robo on their growth cones from the start.

scenes.tts: Axons that do cross carry high levels of Robo only after they have crossed.
scenes.visual: A commissural growth cone with few receptors while crossing, many after.
scenes.narration: Axons that do cross carry high levels of Robo only after they have crossed.

scenes.tts: Picture the ladder stained for Robo protein. The rails are bright. They hold ipsilateral axons and axons already across.
scenes.visual: Ladder recoloured as a Robo stain: rails glow brightly.
scenes.narration: Picture the ladder stained for Robo protein. The rails are bright. They hold ipsilateral axons and axons already across.

scenes.tts: The rungs, where axons are crossing, are much dimmer.
scenes.visual: Rungs much dimmer than the rails in the Robo stain, but not black. Arrows point at the dim rungs.
scenes.narration: The rungs, where axons are crossing, are much dimmer.

scenes.tts: The same axon carries little Robo while it crosses, and a lot once it is across. That is what deaf until crossed means. Deaf here means a much weaker response, not none.
scenes.visual: One axon traced through the stain: dim on the rung, bright on the far rail. Caption on screen: deaf until crossed.
scenes.narration: The same axon carries little Robo while it crosses, and a lot once it is across. That is what deaf until crossed means. Deaf here means a much weaker response, not none.
